--- title: "Assignment 3" editor: visual format: html: code-fold: true code-summary: "Code" --- ::: {.cell} ::: ## Median Household Income Map ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(acs_wide) + geom_sf(aes(fill = incomeE), color = NA) + scale_fill_viridis_c( name = "Median HH Income" ) + labs( title = "Median Household Income in Texas", subtitle = "2024 ACS 5-Year Estimates by County", caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau via tidycensus" ) + theme_minimal() + theme( plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"), plot.caption = element_text(size = 8), legend.position = "right" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](assign03_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Poverty Rate: Top and Bottom 10 Counties ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} top10 <- acs_wide |> st_drop_geometry() |> arrange(desc(pov_rate)) |> select(NAME, pov_rate, pov_moe) |> slice_head(n = 10) bottom10 <- acs_wide |> st_drop_geometry() |> arrange(pov_rate) |> select(NAME, pov_rate, pov_moe) |> slice_head(n = 10) top10_table <- top10 |> mutate( pov_rate = sprintf("%.2f%%", pov_rate * 100), pov_moe = sprintf("±%.2f pp", pov_moe * 100) ) |> rename( County = NAME, `Poverty Rate` = pov_rate, `MOE` = pov_moe ) bottom10_table <- bottom10 |> mutate( pov_rate = sprintf("%.2f%%", pov_rate * 100), pov_moe = sprintf("±%.2f pp", pov_moe * 100) ) |> rename( County = NAME, `Poverty Rate` = pov_rate, `MOE` = pov_moe ) ``` :::

Texas Counties with the Highest Poverty Rates

::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |County |Poverty Rate |MOE | |:----------------------|:------------|:---------| |Dimmit County, Texas |41.11% |±8.88 pp | |Zapata County, Texas |38.39% |±6.04 pp | |Zavala County, Texas |33.92% |±9.53 pp | |Starr County, Texas |33.52% |±3.23 pp | |Duval County, Texas |33.27% |±8.40 pp | |Presidio County, Texas |32.00% |±12.78 pp | |Edwards County, Texas |31.87% |±23.24 pp | |Jim Hogg County, Texas |31.43% |±11.15 pp | |Swisher County, Texas |30.10% |±6.90 pp | |Kleberg County, Texas |28.09% |±4.33 pp | ::: :::

Texas Counties with the Lowest Poverty Rates

::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |County |Poverty Rate |MOE | |:-----------------------|:------------|:--------| |Rockwall County, Texas |4.04% |±0.69 pp | |Sterling County, Texas |4.32% |±2.88 pp | |Sutton County, Texas |4.51% |±2.85 pp | |Kendall County, Texas |5.03% |±1.43 pp | |Armstrong County, Texas |5.19% |±2.80 pp | |Foard County, Texas |5.57% |±4.39 pp | |Roberts County, Texas |5.65% |±3.87 pp | |Loving County, Texas |6.06% |±2.52 pp | |Hemphill County, Texas |6.19% |±3.24 pp | |Collin County, Texas |6.23% |±0.35 pp | ::: ::: ## Uncertainty Check ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} uncertainty_pair <- acs_wide |> st_drop_geometry() |> filter(NAME %in% c("Dimmit County, Texas", "Zapata County, Texas")) |> transmute( County = NAME, `Poverty Rate` = sprintf("%.2f%%", pov_rate * 100), MOE = sprintf("±%.2f pp", pov_moe * 100), `Lower Bound` = sprintf("%.2f%%", (pov_rate - pov_moe) * 100), `Upper Bound` = sprintf("%.2f%%", (pov_rate + pov_moe) * 100) ) ``` :::

Uncertainty in Poverty Rate Estimates

::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |County |Poverty Rate |MOE |Lower Bound |Upper Bound | |:--------------------|:------------|:--------|:-----------|:-----------| |Dimmit County, Texas |41.11% |±8.88 pp |32.23% |49.98% | |Zapata County, Texas |38.39% |±6.04 pp |32.35% |44.44% | ::: ::: Dimmit County has an estimated poverty rate of 41.11% with a margin of error of ±8.88 percentage points, while Zapata County has an estimated rate of 38.39% with a margin of error of ±6.04 percentage points. Their confidence intervals overlap substantially. Therefore, although Dimmit County ranks above Zapata County based on the point estimates, the difference should not be interpreted as a clearly established difference in poverty rates because of the uncertainty in the ACS estimates. ## Methods Note I used the 2024 ACS 5-year estimates for Texas counties. I used median household income (B19013_001) for the map and calculated the poverty rate using the number of people below poverty (B17001_002) divided by the poverty universe (B17001_001). I also kept the margins of error because ACS estimates include sampling uncertainty. The poverty-rate margin of error was calculated using moe_prop(). The results show that county rankings should be interpreted carefully because counties with similar estimates may have overlapping confidence intervals. ## AI Use Appendix ChatGPT was used for troubleshooting selected R code and clarifying parts of the ACS analysis, including poverty-rate and margin-of-error calculations. I executed the code, reviewed the outputs, and made the final decisions about the tables, map, and written interpretation.
